title: Upgrade Emailer Light to Ripe
subtitle: Ripe 1.3.5 | Beginner guide for Light 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 through 1.2.11

blocks.text: Upgrade with the private Ripe 1.3.5 setup file. Your Light administrator becomes an Owner and keeps the same password. Accept the validated upgrade after verification. Successful acceptance retires only this installer’s hold; existing owner pauses remain and actual readiness still blocks sending.

Ubuntu 26.04 uses its maintained distribution PHP 8.5 packages; no external PHP source is added. A compatible existing MariaDB 10.11 or 11.8 service is reused without a major upgrade. Setup adds a dedicated Emailer PHP-FPM pool and keeps existing website pools, PHP alternatives and Virtualmin-managed websites in place. Missing PHP extension packages add their standard extension configuration; existing PHP settings are retained and shared PHP services are not restarted.

Ubuntu 26.04.1 / Virtualmin coexistence uses a spare Emailer hostname and preserves the existing Virtualmin domains and PHP pools. Setup creates its own Apache site; it does not register a Virtualmin domain. Keep that site under Emailer installer management. Light 1.2.4 and 1.2.6 on Ubuntu 26.04 upgrade directly to Ripe 1.3.5; the original Light signing identity, administrator credentials and installation identity are retained. Delivery remains held until the guided readiness acceptance.

Ubuntu 26.04.1 HTTPS acceptance used a local ACME server with real HTTP challenge validation and strict certificate/name verification. Public certificate issuance remains unverified because no dedicated non-production hostname and DNS authority were available. Customer setup uses the normal public ACME service; DNS must point to the server and Apache must be reachable on ports 80 and 443.

blocks.text: Use the Ripe 1.3.5 installer for original Light 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and signed 1.2.0 through 1.2.11. The installer authenticates each explicit source with the established Light identity and checks its exact schema. Native Ripe 1.0.5 first requires the published one-time 1.3.4 repair; other supported native releases retain their direct update route. There is no general Ripe-to-Light downgrade.

Use Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 amd64/systemd with Apache, or Debian 13 with Nginx, PHP 8.4 (PHP 8.5 on Ubuntu 26.04) and supported MariaDB 10.11/11.8. Ubuntu 22.04 fresh installations use an isolated MariaDB 10.11.19 beside any existing host database. The installer discovers protected standard settings under /etc/emailer-light or /etc/emailer, a dedicated application database account, private/key storage and an existing trusted HTTPS hostname without a custom port/subfolder. A dedicated Emailer virtual-host file must not also serve unrelated routes or applications. Unknown customized targets stop before handoff; keep their existing configuration. The automatic handoff requires the recorded dedicated Emailer PHP-FPM service so it can drain only this application. A shared/custom PHP service is preserved and rejected before hold or website mutation; use the operator reference for a supervised quiescent handoff.
1. Prepare for maintenance

Finish intentional sending and allow a short maintenance period. Keep the current HTTPS address and signing keys. Know the existing administrator login and password. If the database needs a separate administrator sign-in, have it ready for the hidden conditional prompt. Setup itself pauses delivery, waits for in-flight work, backs up and verifies recovery material, and fences the old application account. No migration commands or service files need to be written.
2. Download and start Ripe setup

While signed in with access, download emailer-ripe-1.3.5-setup.run from the official private release, or use an authorized private copy. Upload that one file to the existing server through your provider's file-transfer facility. Do not put a GitHub token in a shell command. In the folder containing the file, run:
sudo sh emailer-ripe-1.3.5-setup.run

Initial trust comes from the official HTTPS or authorized private delivery channel. Embedded established signing identities authenticate the Ripe package and all ten supported Light predecessor packages. You do not need to assemble verifier source, sidecars, version arguments or commit hashes.
3. Select and upgrade

If asked about an existing Light installation, choose Upgrade this Light installation to Ripe. If both standard installations are found, select the intended address when asked. A custom or unrecognized target stops without adoption. Check the displayed Light version and address, then choose Upgrade with verified recovery material. Wait for named progress and validation. Retain the printed recovery location.

blocks.caption: Recorded Ubuntu 26.04 / Virtualmin upgrade from Light 1.2.4 to Ripe 1.3.1. The guided Upgrade and Accept controls are retained in 1.3.4.

blocks.text: If interrupted, start the same file and choose Recover an interrupted upgrade before retrying. If the message says conversion committed, follow its Accept instruction. Never delete operation journals or edit migration records to retry.
4. Accept the validated upgrade, then sign in

items: After the automatic validation succeeds, start the same setup file again and choose Accept a validated upgrade. This completes the host handoff and reopens sign-in. The public site stays under maintenance until this action; delivery remains held separately.
Open the existing HTTPS login address and use your unchanged administrator login and password. Old sessions are revoked; the account is now an Owner.

Check campaigns, templates, assets, recipient snapshots, delivery/tracking history, suppressions and existing links. Campaign-owned Light recipients remain campaign-owned; no contacts or list memberships are manufactured.

blocks.text: The transition preserves the password hash, installation identity, SMTP credentials and encryption/token contexts, relevant backups and required audit history. No campaign is approved or newsletter sent as an upgrade side effect. After acceptance, recovery cannot be replayed as a downgrade.
5. Complete security and mail checks

Light upgrades start Ripe at High security with MFA unenrolled. Open Settings & tools > MFA, confirm your credentials, start enrollment, add its setup key to an authenticator app, save the recovery codes privately and confirm a current code. Do not share that secret screen.

blocks.caption: MFA enabled after enrollment, without exposing recovery material.

blocks.text: Open Mail settings. Existing SMTP settings should be retained. Choose Test saved connection to validate the retained TLS and sign-in without sending. When editing settings, Test connection without sending uses the visible current fields; an unsaved success requires an explicit Save SMTP settings. Connection tests work while delivery is held. If Light never had SMTP, you can keep preparing drafts and add it later. Sending a test message is a separate explicit action with a shown destination and respects the delivery hold.
6. Resume when ready

Inspect approved and scheduled work before completing MFA or SMTP: previously enabled delivery may continue when the actual readiness requirement clears. A successful Accept has already retired its own installer hold. If Doctor reports an independent owner pause or unknown legacy intent, review that work, choose Resume delivery after reviewing readiness and answer yes. Resume does not approve drafts or retry failed messages.

blocks.caption: Recorded guided Ripe acceptance output; the same controls remain available in 1.3.4. Sign in and complete MFA, then review Doctor before choosing Resume delivery.

blocks.text: If you are not ready, exit; drafting remains available. Keep recovery material after acceptance.
If something stops

head: Situation
Action
rows: Let the current message finish and retry. Never reset claims manually.
Retain source/recovery files and use the original official package. Do not replace signing keys or migration records.
Choose Recover, verify the restored source, then retry.
Choose Accept a validated upgrade. A completed operation cannot be downgraded by recovery.
Open Doctor, complete MFA/mail settings and resolve the named finding, then retry Resume.

blocks.text: Continue with the Ripe manual. Use the operator reference for exceptional host and recovery cases.
Installer holds and owner pauses

A successful operation releases only its own temporary installer hold after runtime verification and any required Accept action. An independent owner pause or another operation hold remains. Doctor reports the actual MFA, SMTP or other readiness requirement instead of calling a completed installation unfinished. Completing a requirement can allow previously approved due work to continue if the owner already enabled delivery; inspect that work before changing readiness.

An interrupted or recovered operation retains its operation identifier, lifecycle and Finish or Recover action. Use the same verified setup and retained recovery material. Failed and uncertain messages are never retried by completion. An unattributed legacy hold remains unknown until its owner explicitly reviews and resumes it; a zero delivery flag alone never proves installer ownership.
Scan an authenticator QR code privately

After confirming current credentials for MFA management, choose Start or restart enrollment. In a standard authenticator choose Add account and Scan QR code; scan the displayed code. If scanning is unavailable, choose manual entry and copy the adjacent setup key. Both represent the same account. Store recovery codes privately and confirm a current six-digit code. QR generation happens locally; no external QR service is contacted. Do not share or capture the enrollment screen. Existing enrolled accounts keep their factor and do not enrol again.
